R001.text:
H003 gives ell=λ as integers, hence n=ell+1>0; we use ell for the nonnegative highest weight. Define t_r=y^r v. H005 gives t_0=v, h t_0=ell t_0 and x t_0=0. Induct on a natural r. Temporarily assume L1: h t_r=(ell−2r)t_r and, for r≥1, x t_r=r(ell−r+1)t_{r−1}, with x t_0=0 separately. From hy=yh−2y one gets h t_{r+1}=(ell−2r−2)t_{r+1}. From xy=yx+h, for r≥1,
x t_{r+1}=y x t_r+h t_r=[r(ell−r+1)+ell−2r]t_r=(r+1)(ell−r)t_r.
For r=0 the same result is x y v=y x v+h v=ell v. This proves the step and discharges L1. Natural induction proves the stated h and x formulas for every r; scalar subtractions here are in ℤ and then ℂ.

For each i∈I, iterate F001 to obtain
x^i t_i=[∏_{s=1}^i s(ell−s+1)]v=i!·[ell(ell−1)⋯(ell−i+1)]v.
Every factor is a positive integer for 1≤s≤i≤ell, so its complex image is nonzero; the empty product for i=0 is 1. H005 supplies v≠0. Hence t_i≠0. Since i!≠0 in ℂ, e_i=t_i/i!≠0, and F001 gives h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For i,j∈I, equality of these complex weights forces 2(i−j)=0 and hence i=j in characteristic zero.

Apply M001 to the ℂ-vector space V, endomorphism h, eigenvalue function i↦ell−2i on I, and family e. A complex vector space is torsion-free over the integral domain ℂ: multiplying an equation in which a nonzero scalar annihilates a vector by the scalar's inverse forces that vector to be zero. F002 supplies injectivity and all nonzero eigenvector equations. Thus e is complex-linearly independent.

The given complex dimension in H004 is λ+1=ell+1=n by F001. The module is finite-dimensional by that given dimension. The finite set I has n elements. Apply M002 to F003 and |I|=dim_ℂ V to obtain span_ℂ(e)=V. Together with independence, this says e is a complex basis.

F001 gives h t_{ell+1}=(−ell−2)t_{ell+1}. Using F004, define its unique coordinates q_i by t_{ell+1}=∑_{i∈I}q_i e_i. The eigenvector equation and the basis equations give q_i[(ell−2i)−(−ell−2)]=0 for every i. The bracket is 2(ell+1−i), a nonzero complex scalar since i≤ell. Consequently every q_i=0, and t_{ell+1}=0. Since t_{r+1}=y t_r, induction gives t_r=0 for all r>ell.

Divide the F001 formulas by i!, using the nonzero complex factorials, and use F005. This gives x e_0=0, x e_i=(ell−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤ell; y e_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<ell and y e_ell=0; h e_i=(ell−2i)e_i. Iterating the x formula r times for r≤i accumulates (ell−i+1)⋯(ell−i+r)=(ell−i+r)!/(ell−i)!. Divide by r! in ℂ, and apply M005 with nb=ell−i+r,kb=r to identify this as binom(ell−i+r,r). Iterating y for i+r≤ell accumulates (i+1)⋯(i+r)=(i+r)!/i!; M005 with nb=i+r,kb=r yields binom(i+r,r) after division by r!. Both bounds kb≤nb hold by natural addition. If r>i, the x iterate reaches e_0 and is then killed; if i+r>ell, the y iterate reaches e_ell and is then killed. The case r=0 gives identity, including all empty products. These are precisely the claimed X,Y formulas, together with the basis F004 and conversion F001.

R002.text: For every j∈I apply M005 to nb=ell,kb=j, obtaining c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!. Since ell!>0 and both factorials are positive integers, c_j>0. Apply M005 also to kb=ell−j. The two factorial products j!(ell−j)! and (ell−j)!j! coincide; cancel their positive value to get binom(ell,ell−j)=binom(ell,j)=c_j.

Using the basis e from N001 define E_ij as stated. If k<ell, X_ell e_k=0; while X_ell e_ell=e_0 and Y_ell e_0=e_ell. Thus Q=Y_ell X_ell=E_{ell,ell}. N001 also gives X_{ell−i}e_ell=e_i, its coefficient being binom(ell−i,ell−i)=1. For i,j,k∈I, compute Q Y_{ell−j}e_k. If k<j, this is killed by Q because the lowered index k+ell−j is below ell; if k>j, the Y iterate is already zero past the end of the string. If k=j, it is binom(ell,ell−j)e_ell=c_j e_ell by F001. Therefore A_ij=X_{ell−i}QY_{ell−j}=c_j E_ij on the whole complex space, since equality on a basis implies equality of linear maps.

Evaluation on e shows E_ij E_kl=E_il if j=k and zero otherwise, and ∑_i E_ii=Id_V. Substitute F002: A_ij A_kl=c_j A_il if j=k and zero otherwise, since when j=k the product is c_j c_l E_il. Finite product decomposition gives C=c_i d_i for each i. Hence ∑_i d_i A_ii=∑_i C E_ii=C Id_V. By H006 every factor defining A_ij preserves M, so a_ij is its ℤ-linear restriction. For any vector of M the two sides of each integer identity have equal images in V; the inclusion M→V is injective, so the product and sum identities hold in End_ℤ(M). This restriction uses only integer coefficients, with no assertion that E preserves M and no rational scalar action on M.

For every natural r, definitions give r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r in End_ℂ(V), since r! is nonzero in ℂ. H006 ensures all these maps preserve M, including X_1=x and Y_1=y. Restricting the equalities through the injective inclusion gives r! X_r^M=(x^M)^r and r! Y_r^M=(y^M)^r on M. H005 gives h=xy−yx, so h preserves M and h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M. With F001–F003 these prove all statements of the output. When ell=0, I has the single member 0, 0!=1, c_0=C=d_0=1, and Q=A_00=Id_V by the basis computation; all corresponding lattice identities remain valid.

R003.text: By H003, the integer image of ell is λ, and ell<p; n=ell+1>0. H006 supplies an integer basis of M whose images form a complex basis of V. H004 says the latter space has finite dimension λ+1=n. Thus that basis has exactly n members (the finite-dimensional basis cardinality property), and reindexing by I gives an I-indexed paired basis. In particular there exists such a ℤ-basis of M. No property of the divided-power coordinates e as lattice vectors is being used.

Choose b from F001. Let β=b.baseChange K, a K-basis of T. M003, with the canonical ℤ-algebra structure of K, identifies β_i=1⊗b_i for every i∈I. Apply M006 to this finite K-basis: dim_K T=|I|=n. It spans with finitely many members, so T is finite-dimensional. Since n>0, the index 0 belongs to I; β_0≠0, for a zero basis vector would contradict independence using coefficient 1≠0 in the field K. Therefore T is nonzero.

Fix arbitrary ℤ-endomorphisms f,g of M, z∈ℤ, α∈K and m∈M. Use M007 to obtain hat(f)(α⊗m)=α⊗f(m). Pure tensors span T: define the integer coordinates zcoef of m by m=∑_{i∈I} zcoef_i b_i in the basis b and expand α⊗m=∑_i (zcoef_i α)(1⊗b_i) by additivity and balance. Equivalently β in F002 spans. On an arbitrary pure tensor,
hat(f)hat(g)(α⊗m)=α⊗f(g(m)),
hat(f+g)(α⊗m)=α⊗(f(m)+g(m)),
hat(zf)(α⊗m)=α⊗(z f(m))=(zα)⊗f(m).
The same formula for the identity fixes every pure tensor. Equality on spanning pure tensors thus proves preservation of composition, addition, integer scalar multiplication and identity by hat. Finite sums and powers follow by induction. No injectivity or faithfulness of scalar extension is assumed.

For every natural r≤ell, F001 gives r<p. Apply M004 with Ab=K,pb=p,rb=r using H001,H002. The scalar r! is a unit, hence is nonzero in K; in particular ell!≠0. For each j∈I apply M005 with nb=ell,kb=j and cast the identity into K:
(c_j mod K)·(j! mod K)·((ell−j)! mod K)=(ell! mod K)≠0.
If c_j had zero image, the left side would vanish, a contradiction. Hence every c_j has nonzero image. Since K is a field, their finite product, the image of C, is nonzero.

Apply F003 to the integer identities in N002. The extended product relation is hat(a_ij)hat(a_kl)=(c_j mod K)hat(a_il) for j=k, and zero otherwise. By definition F_ij=(c_j mod K)^{-1}hat(a_ij). For j≠k the product F_ij F_kl is zero. For j=k it is
(c_j mod K)^{-1}(c_l mod K)^{-1}(c_j mod K)hat(a_il)=(c_l mod K)^{-1}hat(a_il)=F_il,
using F004 for cancellation. Extend ∑_i d_i a_ii=C Id_M to T. Since C=c_i d_i and c_i,C have nonzero images, (C mod K)^{-1}(d_i mod K)=(c_i mod K)^{-1}. Multiplying the extended sum by (C mod K)^{-1} gives ∑_i F_ii=Id_T. This proves genuine matrix units without reducing a complex coordinate basis.

Extend the factorial identities from N002 using F003. For each natural r≤ell this gives (r! mod K)X̂_r=x̂^r and (r! mod K)Ŷ_r=ŷ^r. Invert the nonzero factorials from F004 to obtain X̂_r=(r! mod K)^{-1}x̂^r and Ŷ_r=(r! mod K)^{-1}ŷ^r. Extending h^M=x^M y^M−y^M x^M gives ĥ=x̂ŷ−ŷx̂. F001,F002,F004,F005 and these identities give every clause of the output; none depends on the particular paired basis b chosen for the dimension argument.

R004.text: Construct s:U→T by m⊗α↦α⊗m and t:T→U by α⊗m↦m⊗α. Each assignment is additive in each argument. For z∈ℤ, (zm)⊗α=m⊗(zα) is sent to α⊗(zm)=(zα)⊗m, exactly the balance relation in T; the reverse check is identical. The tensor universal property therefore gives additive maps, which are K-linear for the scalar action on the K factor. Both composites fix every pure tensor, hence are identities since pure tensors generate the tensor spaces. For any ℤ-endomorphism f of M, s(f(m)⊗α)=α⊗f(m)=hat(f)(s(m⊗α)) by N003. Thus s,t are inverse K-linear maps intertwining every induced lattice operator.

Fix any K-subspace W of T and assume L1: W is invariant under x̂ and ŷ. The identity preserves W. Inductively, if the r-th power of either operator preserves W, applying that operator once more shows its (r+1)-st power preserves W. Thus all their natural powers preserve W. By N003 and closure under K-scalar multiplication, W is invariant under X̂_r,Ŷ_r for every r≤ell. N002 expresses a_ij as the composition of the four restrictions X_{ell−i},Y_ell,X_ell,Y_{ell−j}. Scalar extension preserves this composition by N003. All four indices lie between 0 and ell, so W is invariant under hat(a_ij), then under its scalar multiple F_ij. Discharge L1 and quantify over W: every x̂,ŷ-invariant subspace of T is invariant under every F_ij.

Define G_ij=t F_ij s. Because st=Id_T and ts=Id_U from F001, multiplication and the sum relation in N003 transport to G_ij G_kl=G_il for j=k and zero otherwise, and ∑_i G_ii=Id_U. The same K-linear equivalence transports nonzeroness, finite-dimensionality and dim T=n from N003 to U. For any K-subspace of U invariant under its original induced x,y operators, its image under s is invariant under x̂,ŷ by F001; F002 makes that image invariant under every F_ij. Applying t proves the original subspace invariant under every G_ij. The commutator identity for ĥ in N003 and the intertwinings show that the transported h is exactly the original induced h. H005, H006 and N002 ensure all lattice restrictions exist, so D008 gives precisely the prescribed L_K action. We have thus constructed the claimed family for the original U=M⊗_ℤ K.

R005.text: Fix arbitrary F0,n0,U0,G0,W0 as declared. Assume L1: n0>0, U0 is finite-dimensional over F0 with dimension n0, for all a0,b0,c0,d0∈Fin(n0), G0_{a0,b0} G0_{c0,d0}=G0_{a0,d0} when b0=c0 and zero otherwise, ∑_i G0_ii=Id_U0, and W0 is invariant under the entire G0 family. If W0=0, the required zero-or-whole alternative already holds. In the other branch assume L2: W0≠0. Then there exists w∈W0 with w≠0, since otherwise every member would be zero and W0 would be the zero subspace.
Choose w∈W0 with w≠0 from F001. Evaluating ∑_j G0_jj=Id_U0 at w yields ∑_j G0_jj w=w. If every term were zero, the sum would be zero, contradicting w≠0. Thus there exists j∈Fin(n0) with G0_jj w≠0.

Choose j from F002, and put u=G0_jj w. Invariance gives u∈W0, and u≠0. The multiplication law gives G0_jj u=u by idempotence. Define uvec_i=G0_ij u for every i∈Fin(n0); all uvec_i belong to W0. To prove independence fix arbitrary coefficients coef and assume L3: ∑_i coef_i uvec_i=0. For arbitrary k∈Fin(n0), apply G0_jk. Its product with G0_ij is zero when k≠i, and is G0_jj when k=i. Thus G0_jk uvec_i=0 for i≠k, while G0_jk uvec_k=G0_jj u=u. Linearity reduces the relation to coef_k u=0. Since u≠0 over the field F0, coef_k=0: if nonzero, multiplication by its inverse would force u=0. Every coefficient vanishes. Discharge L3; this proves that uvec is linearly independent.

Apply M002 to Fb=F0,Vb=U0,Jb=Fin(n0),zb=uvec. F003 gives independence; L1 gives finite-dimensionality and |Fin(n0)|=n0=dim_F0 U0. The family spans U0. Since W0 contains its members by F003 and is a subspace, W0 contains their span, hence W0=U0 in the L2 branch. Discharge L2 by combining this branch with the already settled W0=0 branch; the dichotomy holds under L1. Discharge L1 into the quantified implication, and universally quantify the arbitrary data. This proves the claimed universal dichotomy, for any field, without an algebraic-closure condition.

R006.text: N004 supplies a nonzero finite-dimensional U of dimension n>0 and an I-indexed matrix-unit family; choose that family as G_U with its full asserted invariance property. Here I=Fin(n). These are the required hypotheses for the universal lemma N005 on the original tensor module U.

Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂U, and assume L1: W is invariant under the original induced x,y,h. Its invariance under x,y alone implies invariance under all G_U, by N004. Instantiate N005 with F0=K,n0=n,U0=U,G0=G_U,W0=W. S001 gives the dimension and matrix-unit hypotheses, so W=0 or W=U. Discharge L1 and quantify over W. Together with nonzeroness from N004 this proves the requested irreducibility. H005 and H006 ensure the lattice actions in L_K are defined; invariance under its generators is equivalent to invariance under their K-linear combinations, since W is a K-subspace.

All data remain arbitrary under the original hypotheses. H003 includes λ=0 and p=2; it imposes no algebraic-closure condition on K. The nonnegative integer conversion gives ell=0 when λ=0, so n=1 and N004 yields a nonzero one-dimensional module. When p=2 the permitted λ are 0 and 1, and N004 and N005 apply to both, with no distinct-weight condition in characteristic p. Hence neither boundary case is excluded by any step of this final implication.
